anna.blurb: Your friend in Slovakia. She meets you for coffee, shows you around the city, and chats about daily life.
anna.note: Voice Design. Friendly peer in everyday dialogues.

maria.blurb: An administrator at the language school. She handles course registrations, schedules, and official forms.
maria.note: Voice Design. Older / admin counterpart (registration, forms).

lucia.blurb: A shop assistant in town. She helps customers find items, check prices, and pay at the register.

receptionist.blurb: A front desk receptionist. She greets guests, checks reservations, and answers questions at check-in.

alex.blurb: The learner in everyday dialogues. Alex moves through Bratislava, asks for directions, and orders food.
alex.note: Voice Design. Learner voice for dialogue turns labeled You.

marek.blurb: A friendly coworker and classmate. He chats during work breaks, helps with projects, and plans weekend outings.

waiter.blurb: A café waiter in old town. He takes drink orders, serves pastries, and brings the bill.
waiter.note: Voice Design (eleven_ttv_v3), seventh design, preview 1 kept: designed on a waiter's own table talk, not the learner sample, so he talks instead of reading. The fifth take (5YDe2nLAVwkbKkGii7je) sounded like a boy and is kept for a child character.

guide.blurb: Your learning assistant robot. Introduces new grammar patterns and reads lesson vocabulary aloud.
guide.note: Voice Design. Key phrases (keyPhraseCharacterId) — not dictionary Neutral.

narrator.blurb: The site host robot. Pronounces dictionary words and reads public signs, announcements, and scene notes.
narrator.note: Same voice as dictionary Neutral. Unknown-speaker fallback.

announcer.blurb: The loudspeaker. Reads out stops and stations on the tram, platform announcements and public notices.
announcer.note: The first Waiter take, which sounds like a tannoy. Never a person on stage.

robot.blurb: Marek's new home robot. He has a plan for everything, says pán and pani to everyone, and is still learning dog.
robot.note: Voice Design, briefed on Domo's own lines at Marek's flat. Custom Voice Design.

dog.blurb: Marek's dog. He barks hello, growls no, and waits by the window at six for Marek.
dog.note: Not a voice: each line's text is a bark. A line with a recording uses it (CC0, see content/audio/sounds/README.md); otherwise its prompt in `sounds` goes to ElevenLabs sound generation.

sounds.Haf!: A single friendly bark from a medium-sized family dog, close up in a quiet living room, dry, no music, no voices.
One soft, quiet, gentle bark from a medium-sized family dog, almost a huff, close up in a quiet living room, dry, no music, no voices.
sounds.Haf! Haf!: Two quick happy barks from a medium-sized dog running on grass in a park, close up, no music, no voices.
sounds.Haf! Haf! Haf!: Three excited, overjoyed barks from a medium-sized family dog greeting its owner at the door, close up indoors, no music, no voices.
sounds.Vrrr…: A short low warning growl from a medium-sized family dog, wary rather than angry, close up in a quiet living room, no barking, no music, no voices.
sounds.Kňu…: A medium-sized dog whimpering softly once, a sad lonely whine, close up in a quiet living room, no barking, no music, no voices.
